title: The SQL workbench refuses a syntax error as a read-only violation instead of reporting the parse error

criteria.given: a logged-in ROLE_SQL_EXEC caller posting a statement no grammar can parse and no lexical allowance covers (select * from 'account' — a string literal where an identifier belongs; and a typo, selec 1)
criteria.then: the workbench still refuses it with 400 — the guard stays fail-closed — but the response code is SQL_SYNTAX_ERROR and the message is a syntax error carrying the standard grammar's position and a short reason, and it still says only read-only statements can run; it is not READ_ONLY_VIOLATION

criteria.given: the same caller posting a genuine write (DELETE FROM customer)
criteria.then: the workbench refuses it with 400 READ_ONLY_VIOLATION — today's wording and code for a real write are unchanged

criteria.given: the same caller posting a statement with a quote still open at end of input (select * from account where name = 'o)
criteria.then: the workbench refuses it with 400 SQL_SYNTAX_ERROR and the message names the unterminated string or identifier quote

criteria.given: the workbench allowlist as the backend enforces it (SELECT / WITH / VALUES / TABLE / DESCRIBE, plus the lexical SHOW / DESC allowance)
criteria.then: a parsed but non-query statement (CALL some_proc(1)) is refused with a message that names that allowlist — the surface the UI hint text must match

steps.name: a quoted string where an identifier belongs is refused as a syntax error with the parser's position, not as a read-only violation

code.because: a statement that cannot be parsed is a syntax problem, not a permission problem

message.matches: (?=[\s\S]*SQL syntax error at line 1, column 15)(?=[\s\S]*table names are identifiers — use account or "account", not 'account')(?=[\s\S]*Only read-only statements can be run)
message.because: the message carries the standard grammar's position, a short reason for the single-quote mistake, and still says only read-only statements can run

steps.name: a typo (selec 1) is refused as a syntax error with the parser's position

message.contains: SQL syntax error at line 1, column 1
message.because: the message carries the standard grammar's position for the typo too

steps.name: a genuine write is still refused with READ_ONLY_VIOLATION and today's wording
an unterminated quote gets its own message, not the generic read-only one

message.matches: (?=[\s\S]*Unterminated string or identifier quote)(?=[\s\S]*Only read-only statements can be run)
message.because: the quote never closed — the message says so and still refuses the statement

steps.name: a parsed non-query statement names the backend's allowlist (the surface the UI hint must match)

message.because: the backend's own allowlist wording — the UI hint text says the same things it allows
